claim_boundary: This proves a uniform computability barrier for a registered conservative strict-FIX class. It preserves efficient honesty, nonzero complete noise, local coordinate atoms, fixed vector messages, and polylog verifier resources. It is a candidate negative resolution only if the parent quantifies over arbitrary computable uniform family encodings. It does not decide the missing representation grammar, rule out noncomputable characterizations, or supply external review.

fixed_game_specification.exhibited_verifier: query the first coordinate where the two vectors differ and select the matching advocate
fixed_game_specification.ideal_oracle: H_e,d(z,i)=z_i while e has not halted within d steps, otherwise H_e,d(z,i)=0
fixed_game_specification.legal_protocol_scope: uniform randomized verifier and advocate algorithms may choose actions only inside this fixed one-round vector interface
fixed_game_specification.message_alphabet: P_b sends one d-bit vector of parity b; malformed messages lose
fixed_game_specification.message_order: simultaneous fixed vector messages, then one verifier query
fixed_game_specification.noise: one BSC(1/5) response; nonzero and completely specified
fixed_game_specification.prover_information: both claim-labelled advocates observe z and the public input
fixed_game_specification.public_input: unary depth d>=2 and fixed machine-family identifier
fixed_game_specification.refutation_relation: when the oracle is active, one ideal coordinate answer refutes a claimant whose vector disagrees there; when inactive no atom set is declared refuting
fixed_game_specification.semantic_atoms: coordinate queries a_i returning one local bit
fixed_game_specification.uniform_gap: worst-case correct-side selection probability minus worst-case false-side selection probability over worlds, legal adversaries, coins, and noise
fixed_game_specification.verifier_information: the verifier sees the public input, messages, coins, and its one noisy oracle response, but not z

prior_exact_boundary_audit.finite_explicit_boundary: each supplied finite game has an exact TV/sequence-form certificate
prior_exact_boundary_audit.uniform_program_boundary: deciding eventual constant gap across arbitrary computable generators is undecidable

reduction_audit.proof_basis: many-one reduction from NONHALT; finite fixtures validate mechanics but do not prove undecidability

resolution_effect.canonical_negative_route_candidate: yes, if v0.1 includes arbitrary computable uniform task-family encodings
resolution_effect.why_not_unconditional: v0.1 does not freeze the representation grammar for uniform task families, and undecidable membership does not rule out noncomputable mathematical characterizations

class_definition.finite_prefix_convention: ignored, as in standard asymptotic complexity classes
class_definition.instance_encoding: Turing-machine index generating a uniform computable family of strict fixed interfaces
class_definition.membership: there exist uniform in-interface algorithms and constants c>0,N such that every depth d>=N has completeness/soundness gap at least c
class_definition.name: WV-FIX-UCOMP
class_definition.source_faithfulness: conservative strict-FIX successor lane; arbitrary computable uniform encodings are not expressly excluded by v0.1

theorem.finite_boundary: every fixed explicit depth remains exactly decidable by terminal-law TV or sequence-form certificates
theorem.positive_certificate_barrier: the positive index set is not recursively enumerable
theorem.quantifier_scope: the upper bounds range over every legal uniform protocol inside the fixed vector interface, not only the exhibited first-difference verifier
theorem.undecidability: no total algorithm decides WV-FIX-UCOMP membership for arbitrary program-encoded uniform families
theorem.uniform_membership_equivalence: G_e is in WV-FIX-UCOMP iff machine e never halts
